sentences.text: Clara lived in a big house in London a long time ago.
The year was 1815.
She was a young woman, and she loved books more than anything.
She did not like big parties or new dresses.
Her mother, Lady Eleanor, had a different plan.
'Clara, this is an important year,' she said every day.
'You must find a good husband.
He must be a rich and important man.'
Clara was sad when she heard this.
She wanted to study science, but women could not go to a university then.
Yesterday, they went to a very big ball.
Many people were there.
The music was loud, and the lights were bright.
Young women laughed and danced with handsome men.
But Clara was bored.
She felt lonely in the big room.
'Go and dance,' her mother said.
But Clara did not want to.
She quietly walked away from the ballroom.
She found a quiet room down a long hallway.
It was a beautiful library.
There were hundreds of books.
She felt happy and safe there.
She took a book about astronomy from a shelf.
She loved to learn about the stars.
Suddenly, a man's voice said, 'That is an excellent book.'
Clara jumped.
She looked up.
A kind-looking man was standing near her.
He was the Duke of Alistair.
Everyone knew he was very important, but he was not in the ballroom.
He was here, in the library.
'I like stars,' Clara said quietly.
'They are more interesting than this party.'
The Duke smiled a big smile.
'I agree,' he said.
'I am reading a book about plants.
It is very interesting.'
They talked for a long time about science and ideas.
Clara felt very happy.
She was not lonely now.
Later, her mother found her.
Lady Eleanor was angry.
'Clara! What are you doing?
You should not be in here!
You must talk to important men!'
she said.
The Duke spoke.
'Madam, your daughter is a very smart woman.
Our conversation was better than any dance.'
He then looked at Clara.
'I have a new telescope at my house.
You should see it soon.'
Clara’s eyes were wide.
A telescope!
It was a wonderful idea.
Her mother was quiet.
Clara smiled at the Duke.
He was a true friend.
Perhaps her future in London can be different.
Perhaps she can have books and a friend too.
